description: Team Chuijhal is a multidisciplinary collective of innovators bridging the gap between orbit and earth. By harnessing NASA’s advanced Earth observation data—including multispectral imagery, climate models, and hydrological telemetry—our team is building actionable solutions for modern agriculture. We are dedicated to transforming complex space data into intuitive tools that empower farmers to optimize resource use, combat climate stress, and secure sustainable food systems for the future

Agro Shift Rotate: Bringing Agricultural Intelligence Closer to Every Field

Project Overview

Agro Shift Rotate is a Bengali-first, location-aware agricultural intelligence platform designed to make geospatial, environmental, and agricultural information more accessible and understandable for farmers and agricultural stakeholders in Bangladesh. The project explores how Earth observation data, regional agricultural datasets, geographic information systems, and field-level mapping workflows can be brought together in a single digital platform to support better agricultural awareness and informed decision-making.

Agriculture is closely connected to environmental conditions that continuously change across seasons and geographic locations. Temperature, rainfall, humidity, solar radiation, soil properties, water availability, salinity, and land-use patterns all influence agricultural production. However, these different types of information are often scattered across separate datasets, technical platforms, maps, and scientific resources. Farmers and local agricultural stakeholders may find it difficult to access, interpret, and connect this information with their actual farmland.
details:
Agro Shift Rotate: Bringing Agricultural Intelligence Closer to Every Field

Agro Shift Rotate is a Bengali-first, location-aware agricultural intelligence platform designed to make environmental and agricultural information more accessible to farmers in Bangladesh. It connects field-level information, regional agricultural datasets, and NASA Earth observation resources through a unified digital platform.

What it does and how it works: Users can enable GPS to identify their current location, navigate an interactive map, and manually draw, edit, and confirm their agricultural field boundaries. The platform calculates the selected parcel area and uses the confirmed field information as the foundation for its agricultural workflow. Its regional data architecture organizes information related to climate, soil, water, salinity, hydrology, land use, crop calendars, and crop rotation, while clearly communicating data availability and limitations.

Agro Shift Rotate integrates monthly climate information from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation. These data provide broader environmental context for agricultural analysis. It also uses NASA GIBS to display MODIS Terra 8-day vegetation index imagery, offering regional vegetation context through satellite visualization. Additional features include agricultural condition exploration, crop comparison workflows, and an irrigation water-balance demonstration using clearly identified synthetic scenarios.

Benefits and intended impact: The platform aims to reduce the gap between complex environmental datasets and the practical information needs of farmers. Its Bengali-first interface improves accessibility, while location-aware field registration helps connect agricultural information with the user's selected land. By organizing regional datasets and making missing or uncertain information visible, Agro Shift Rotate encourages transparent, data-informed agricultural exploration. Its long-term vision is to support precision agriculture, strengthen regional agricultural information systems, and contribute to more accessible agricultural decision support in Bangladesh.

Tools and technologies: The project was developed using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with a modular application architecture and a Node.js-based data-serving workflow. It uses browser geolocation, interactive mapping and geospatial boundary handling, JSON-based regional datasets, and custom agricultural data adapters. NASA POWER provides climate information through its API, while NASA GIBS supplies satellite imagery through web mapping services. Development and testing tools include Git, GitHub, QGIS, and automated JavaScript tests.

Creativity and innovation: Agro Shift Rotate brings several capabilities together in one farmer-oriented workflow: GPS-based field registration, regional agricultural data organization, NASA climate information, satellite vegetation visualization, and agricultural analysis demonstrations. Instead of presenting satellite information as isolated maps, it connects Earth observation resources with field registration and regional agricultural context. Its Bengali-first design and transparent data-availability system make it particularly relevant to the needs of farmers in Bangladesh.

Factors considered: The project prioritizes accessibility, location accuracy, data provenance, scientific transparency, and responsible use of environmental information. It distinguishes between measured, dataset-derived, estimated, farmer-reported, synthetic, and unavailable information. NASA POWER monthly climate data are not presented as daily field observations, and MODIS imagery is not treated as parcel-level measurement. Synthetic irrigation scenarios are explicitly labelled as demonstrations. Irrigation recommendations remain disabled until sufficient local data, independent validation, and agronomic review are available.

Agro Shift Rotate is an evolving prototype built around one central idea: connect Earth observation, location-aware technology, and regional agricultural information to make agricultural intelligence more understandable and accessible to the farmers of Bangladesh.
